text: If unsure, first name the need and check mandatory limits before comparing options.

items: CAP: supported persons; MOB: movement speed, km/h; FP: functional performance on an abstract scale; PRO: resilience on an abstract scale.
COM: information-link range, km; SA: detection methods; REC: equipment-recovery methods; MC: hazard-clearance methods.
All quantities start at zero in the teaching model. Apply signed changes; negative results are not automatically clipped.
Protection Priority: SA 1; COM 25; PRO 10; FP 10; MOB 80; CAP 4.
Long-Range Survey: SA 5; COM 75; PRO 2; FP 4; MOB 120; CAP 3.
People Transport: SA 2; COM 25; PRO 4; FP 2; MOB 100; CAP 10.
Mobile Coordination: SA 4; COM 125; PRO 4; FP 2; MOB 60; CAP 5.
Equipment Recovery: REC 3; SA 2; COM 75; PRO 6; FP 4; MOB 80; CAP 3.
Hazard Clearance: MC 3; SA 1; COM 25; PRO 10; FP 8; MOB 40; CAP 4.
CAP is persons; MOB is km/h; COM is km. Other fields use points or ways.
positive(x) = max(x, 0). floor(x) = largest whole number not greater than x.
Protection Priority = 20*floor(positive(MOB-80)/10) + 20*positive(FP-10).
Long-Range Survey = 20*floor(positive(COM-75)/25) + 20*positive(SA-5).
People Transport = 20*positive(CAP-10) + 20*positive(PRO-4).
Mobile Coordination = 20*positive(CAP-5) + 20*floor(positive(COM-125)/25).
Equipment Recovery = 20*positive(PRO-6) + 40*positive(REC-3).
Hazard Clearance = 20*positive(SA-1) + 40*positive(MC-3).
Purchase cost = sum of actual accepted auction payments.
Profit = a team-selected amount. Ten percent is one spreadsheet example, not a fixed rule.
Final bid = purchase cost + profit.
A recorded-compliant design passes every listed minimum.
Rated points use the exact mission formula, only above the threshold.
Cost per point = final bid / rated points, for positive points.
Digital decision: submitted + compliant + positive score is required for an award. Digital decision: a zero-score compliant bid has no ratio and does not win.
Four phases: plan; bid and buy; total design; present and discuss.
Ten offers per round: capacity, mobility, functional performance, protection, communications, awareness, accessories, and three SE process slots.
Each team wins at most two cards in a round.
Seven to ten rounds are described, with exact team-count mapping not available.
Original rules do not specify bid increments, tie resolution, unsold stock, or full deck.

text: Twelve tests of a good requirement

items: Necessary: responds to a real need. Appropriate: suitable for the required system level.
Unambiguous: one interpretation. Complete: enough detail to act and assess.
Singular: one obligation. Clear: plain and understandable.
Feasible: achievable within known limits. Verifiable: suitable evidence can settle it.
Correct: reflects the intended need. Design-independent: leaves valid solution choice.
Traceable: linked to origin and downstream evidence. Conforming: follows the governing requirement format.
Certification: recognized independent conformity result when certification is required.
Inspection: examination of a feature without special laboratory procedures.
Analysis: justified calculation, model, simulation or formal reasoning.
Demonstration: observed behavior while operating the item.
Description with evidence: supported documents, specifications or records.
Test: controlled performance measurement with recorded results.
Method selection depends on the claim. Verification checks conformance; validation checks intended-use fitness.
